text: Zither HarpHi, boys and girls.Welcome back.I'm Lulu.Have you got everything ready with you?Now, let's begin our class.In the first and second period of this unit,we talked about some characteristics of encyclopedia entries.When we look for information in an encyclopedia,we can find a lot of facts.Here, I've got a question for you.Is it a good idea to use an encyclopedia to learn about tourist destinations?Here, tourist destination means 旅遊目的地.What's your opinion, Joyce?I don't think it's a good idea to look for information about a tourist destination in an encyclopedia.Why not?When we want to visit a place, we would like to know what we can do and see there.We also want to know what's special and how much we should pay.We may need to find out how we can get there and what else can be found around the place.I think a travel book is more helpful, but I do believe there is plenty of useful information about the history of the tourist destination in the encyclopedia.Thank you, Joyce.I can't agree more.Although we can find a lot of helpful information in an encyclopedia, it is not enough for us to plan a wonderful trip.Joyce suggested the travel book.I enjoy watching some travel programs.They not only tell how interesting these places are, but provide us with necessary tips for planning a trip.Now, please watch a clip of a program and tell me what it is probably about.The city of Nanjing was the capital of China for many dynasties, and it has many places of interest that show its long history.Lucas, what is the video probably about?I think it's about travelling in Nanjing.Good.Have you ever been to Nanjing before?Yes, I've been there several times.Where can we go in Nanjing?I've been to Confucius Temple,Xiaolin Mausoleum of Ming Dynasty,Dr.Sun Yansang's Mausoleum,Nanjing City Wall,Presidental Palace and Zijing Mountain.I visited the observatory on the top of Zijing Mountain.I also went on a cruise on Qinghuai River, enjoying the night views along the river.You really know a lot of interesting places in Nanjing.Now, let's try to find out which place the program mainly talks about.Sun Yansang's MausoleumWhat will you learn about in the program?Yes, that's Dr.Sun Yansang's Mausoleum.A mausoleum is a special building made to hold the dead body of an important person.Sun Yansang就是我們熟知的國父,孫中山。他原名孫文,好日新,又好義先。孫義先廣東話的拼音就是Sun Yansang。因為孫中山曾經做過醫生,所以被尊稱為Dr.Sun Yatsang。At Dr.Sun Yatsang's Mausoleum, you can remember the father of the nation.It is a historical site in our country.Can you make a guess what we can learn about the mausoleum from the program?Joyce, please.Maybe we may know where the mausoleum is, how big it is, what we can see and do at the mausoleum.We can also know how much we should pay for the entrance fee.Perhaps there will be an introduction about Dr.Lucas, do you have any other idea?What about when the construction of the mausoleum started and finished?Who designed the building?How it was built?Who looks after the mausoleum now?Are there any other places to visit near mausoleum?Thank you.You both made some predictions about the program.Now, it's time to watch the program together.While you watch, complete task one in your worksheet.Tick the different aspects the program shows us.Are you ready?The city of Nanjing was the capital of China for many dynasties.And it has many places of interest that show its long history.One example is Dr.Sun Yatsang's mausoleum.Sun was a great pioneer in China's history.He helped bring China into a new age in 1911.After Dr.Sun died in 1925, people built a mausoleum for him.The mausoleum is over 80,000 square meters in size.It has a large forest and some beautiful buildings.The government looks after the mausoleum very well.In 1978 and 1986, the government spent 1.2 million yuan repairing the roofs and walls of the buildings.Millions of people come to visit the mausoleum every year.For many years it was free.But since 1992, you must pay an entrance fee.All the money is used to help with the repairs and cleaning of the mausoleum.Behind the mausoleum is the famous Zhejin Mountain.It is 448.9 meters high.You can take a cable car up the mountain.The mausoleum is a beautiful place to visitand to remember this great man.Have you got the answers?The program gives a short introduction about Dr.It tells the mausoleum is in Nanjing.We also know the construction of the mausoleum started just after Dr.Sun died.We know what the mausoleum looks like.We know the government takes good care of it.It also mentions the famous Zhejin Mountain.It's a beautiful place to go to after you pay a visit to the mausoleum.Now, can you put these aspects in the correct order?Now you see the program talks about these six aspects.When the program tells about the location of the mausoleum,it actually gives a brief introduction about Nanjing.When giving an introduction about Dr.Sun,it tells why the mausoleum was built.The next three aspects are about the mausoleum itself.Why does the program talk about Zhejin Mountain?The mausoleum and the mountain are neighbours.The speaker gives some related information about the mausoleum.Here you've got a note about Dr.Sun's mausoleum.Can you figure out what information is missing in the blanks?Let's take the first and the third blanks as examples.For blank 1, what should be put in it, Joyce?I think it should be a noun.It's part of the structure de blah blah off.A noun is missing here.Very good.Before you complete a note, read it carefullyand decide what information is missing in each blank.What about blank 3, Lucas?It seems like a number.A year, I think.I agree with you.Do you need to write the number in words?No, I don't.I just write it in figures.It saves time.You got it.When you hear numbers, don't write them in words.In figures only.Now, read the note by yourself.Are you ready to complete the note?It's task 2 in your worksheet.Sun Yat-sen's mausoleum.It is the highest mountain in China.Now let's check the answers.Look at the second part.Why does the speaker mention the year 1911?It was a great year in Chinese history.The revolution of 1911 took place that year,辛亥革命。Sun was a great leader in the revolution.The second part,Why does the speaker mention the year 1911?The success of the revolution brought China into a republic.That's why Dr.Sun is regarded as the father of the nation.The program doesn't tell us the facts about the mausoleum only.Which sentence in the video shows it's not just an introduction.Lucas, have you noticed anything?I noticed at the end of the program,the speaker says the mausoleum is a beautiful place to visitand to remember the great man.What does this sentence mean to you?I think the speaker wants me and other tourists to visit the mausoleum.Yes, when I watch the video, I have the same feeling.Does this sentence show a fact or his opinion about the mausoleum?In fact, the sentence has got two parts.The first part shows the speaker's feeling about the mausoleum.It looks beautiful.People enjoy beautiful sceneryand the mausoleum is a right place to pay a visit to.The second part shows the mausoleum is the right placeto remember the great man, Dr.Sun Yat-sen.It's a fact.Every year, a lot of people go thereand show their respect to him.Does an encyclopedia entry include a lot of opinions?Of course not.An encyclopedia entry shows two facts only.My next question for you iswhy doesn't the speaker tell how much the entrance fee is?Joyce, what do you think of it?The program is a recommendation on Dr.It mainly tells people what to say and what to do there,although it mentions the entrance fee.The aim is to tell people they have to pay to get in.Besides, the entrance fee may change as time goeswhile the program may be online or on TV for a long time.Good guessing, Joyce.You may get the information about the entrance feeby viewing the official website of Dr.One more question for you to think about.Why does the speaker mention Zijing Mountain in the video?I think the travel program wants people to visit more places in Nanjing.Or maybe there will be another program introducing Zijing Mountain.Smart, Lucas.As a travel program,there should be enough information on a tourist destination.What's your view, Joyce?With the visit in Nanjing,I found Dr.Sun's mausoleum is at the foot of Zijing Mountain.I think the program tells us the location of the mausoleumby telling us Zijing Mountain is just by its side.I agree with you, too.By introducing Zijing Mountain,the program indicates the location of the mausoleumand encourages tourists to visit more places in Nanjing.In fact, when Dr.Sun knew he would soon pass away,he decided the location of his tomb.He wanted to be buried in Nanjingbecause Nanjing was the capital of China at that time.Now it's time for you to introduce the mausoleum.I want you to write an encyclopedia entry about the mausoleum.What does the beginning of an encyclopedia entry usually show?Remember the entries Diogenes and Disney World?Yes, it's a definition.Then what follows?That should be some facts about it,like where it is, how big it is.Also, there should be a brief introduction about its history.Don't forget the present status.That is how it is now.Here, I've got two definitions about the mausoleum.Which one do you choose?Take a look first.I choose the first one.I choose the first one because it states the fact.What about the other one?It is an opinion.Which word shows it is an opinion, Lucas?Wonderful.The word wonderful shows it is an opinion.That's right.So we will use the first option as the beginning of the entry.When we talk about the location,we should not just write it is in Nanjing.You can give a more detailed one like this.Also, we may use it covers an area of to tell the size of the mausoleum.When introducing the present status,you may mention how the government takes care of itand how many people visit it yearly.Now, it's time for you to finish the entry.That is task 3 in your worksheet.Lucas, would you please share your work with us?Lucas has demonstrated a good example of writing an encyclopedia entry.Have you found that Lucas wrote this entry in time order?It's a good introduction about a historical site.Also, Lucas' entry doesn't include the introduction of Dr.Sun's life.If you need to learn more, you can read the related entry.Well done, Lucas.In today's class, we learned that when we introduce a historical place,we can list the facts of it like where it is,how big it is, what the history is,how big it is, what the history is, how it is now.We can also express our own opinions.Opinions help others know more about the placeand even make a picture in mind.With a definition and important facts,we may be able to write an encyclopedia entry.If you include some opinions,you are giving others a recommendation on this site.This is the end of today's class.Don't forget to complete the exercises listed in the homework sheet.Remember to revise your writing in task 3 after class.See you next time.
